$comment: Upstream repositories this fork follows, one entry per source under `sources`. Read and updated by .claude/skills/upstream-review. There is NO git merge-base with the code upstream -- the LFS history rewrite severed it -- so this file is the only durable baseline. Store upstream identifiers only, never a fork commit SHA: fork history has been rewritten before and those SHAs die with it. `skipped` = upstream changes deliberately not taken; `divergences` = upstream files this fork deliberately changes. The parity check (SKILL.md Step 7) fails on any upstream file that differs here and is in neither list.

ws4kp-music.$comment: No release tags: the baseline is a commit on main. Albums are folders; the playlist reader scans only server/music and falls back to server/music/default (no subfolders, no seasonal logic), so adopted albums are flattened into server/music/default under the naming below.
ws4kp-music.naming: <album>--<song>.mp3, all lower case, each space a single dash (latest-observations--rolling-clouds.mp3): the album prefix keeps same-named songs apart (both albums have Rolling Clouds) without a per-file rename list

Current Conditions.source: not this repo: the 192 kbps 2025 copies that shipped in ws4kp server/music/default (4 of them) plus 6 more, tagged by this fork with album "Current Conditions" and artist "WeatherStar 4000+" to match Latest Observations. ws4kp-music at this sha has 128 kbps re-encodes tagged album "Current Conditions".
Current Conditions.decision: keep the 192 kbps copies (user, 2026-10-24): quality over the ~10 MB the re-encodes would save. Do not propose replacing them with the repo's copies.
Current Conditions.bitrate: 192 kbps except First snow, which is 128 kbps: its only original (ws4kp-music 5fed6bc, blob 4a7d01b, byte-identical audio to ours) was 128, and no 192 kbps copy was ever published (checked 2026-10-25)
